sentences.text:
Heard Sri Shyam Shankar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Dharmendra Prasad,
learned counsel for the informant and Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Crime No.0033 of 2024, registered under Section 498A, 323, 313, 504, 506 IPC at Police Station- Gorakhnath, District Gorakhpur with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: The marriage of the informant was solemnized with the applicant as per Hindu rites on 29.06.2020 and the applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry.
There is allegation against the applicant of having forcibly administered some medicine to her leading to her miscarriage.

The FIR was instituted under section 498A, 504, 506,
313, 323 IPC.
4.

The applicant had filed an anticipatory bail application before this Court which was dismissed as infructuous on the prayer of the applicant as Section 313 IPC was deleted by the Investigating Officer,
as such, the applicant had applied for regular bail before the Sessions Judge, Gorakhpur whereby the applicant was granted interim bail.

5. Subsequently, the Investigating Officer has applied for remand under section 313 IPC, as such the applicant had no other option but to withdraw the said application which was dismissed as withdrawn on 24.04.2024.
6. The applicant has again applied for anticipatory bail under the peculiar circumstances of the case.

The said fact has been mentioned in paragraph no.8 of the application as the final report (charge sheet) was submitted against the applicant under sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 IPC only.
7.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that there is no evidence whatsoever under section 313 IPC.
The doctor has also categorically opined that he could not ascertain the cause of miscarriage of the victim.
The allegations against the applicant are vague.
8. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

9. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Supreme Court.
10. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

Let the accused-applicant- Abhishek Kumar Singh be released forthwith in the aforesaid case crime (supra)
on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of trial on furnishing a personal and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the Police Station concerned/court concerned with the following conditions:-
i. that the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
ii. that the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him Abhishek Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 September, 2024
